Subject: Annual token commit options for Greenline AI

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost metrics looked promising for our inference-heavy workflows. Procurement and finance asked me to catalog the annual commit options so we can review with engineering and present to our execs.

High-level asks from our side:
- A clear Starter/Growth/Enterprise matrix (token volumes + net effective discounts)
- How burst/overage works if we exceed committed tokens in a month
- Any credits or protections (rollover, fallback credits) for seasonal spikes
- Contract deliverables: SLA targets, data residency notes, and billing cadence

Can you share a concise proposal we can circulate? Prefer a single PDF and a spreadsheet with the math.

Thanks,
Sophia

Hi Sophia — great to connect. Attached is a short proposal PDF and a working spreadsheet that breaks down unit economics across three anchor tiers. Key points up front:

Attachment: Redwood-Annual-Commit-Proposal-Greenline.pdf (3 pages)
Attachment: commit_pricing_model.xlsx (token math + sample billing schedule)

Proposal highlights (summary):
- Starter: 25M tokens / year — 15% net discount off published hosted per-token, quarterly billing option, aimed at product teams validating critical paths
- Growth: 150M tokens / year — 28% net discount, includes 10% rollover pool and 20% burst cushion above monthly committed rate (billed at discounted overage rate)
- Enterprise: 600M+ tokens / year — 40% net discount, dedicated support SLAs, rollover up to 25% and guaranteed burst capacity for the first 30% over month baseline (credits applied for sustained overage)

Fallback and protections:
- Burst credit: for single-month spikes above baseline, first 20% billed at the Growth/Enterprise overage rate, next 10% compensated via flex credits (applied as a bill credit once per year)
- Rollover: unused committed tokens roll into next month up to the configured rollover pool; annual unused tokens are eligible for a one-time conversion to flex credits (per schedule in spreadsheet)

Open items we should confirm with procurement/finance:
- Preferred billing timing (monthly vs quarterly vs annual prepay)
- Whether Greenline requires a firm SLA credit schedule in the MSA
- Any regulatory/data residency clauses for EU workloads (if applicable)

I looped in Laura from finance for billing cadence and to confirm how flex credits would flow on invoices.

Next step: if this aligns, we can provision a formal term sheet and a HubSpot deal record (I can draft). Would Greenline like a short 30-minute call to walk the spreadsheet?

Best,
Evelyn

Hi Sophia — Rishi here (lead AE on your account). Quick notes from a commercial lens after reviewing Evelyn's draft:

1) Discount curve: we recommend making the Growth tier hinge points a bit more granular for forecasting. Example increments: 75M, 150M, 300M with stepped discounts (22% / 28% / 33%) rather than a single 150M bucket. That helps Greenline model mix changes during ramp.

2) Overage pricing: propose a two-tier overage rate — 50% of published rate up to 30% over baseline, then 80% thereafter; for Enterprise we can cap excessive overage exposure in year 1 via a "safety valve" credit (one-time annual protection).

3) Flex credits: suggest we offer conversion for annual unused tokens into credits at 60% of the hosted list value (per the spreadsheet tab "Flex Credit Calc"). That prevents accounting headaches for both sides.

Laura — can you confirm whether quarterly billing with one-month net terms works, or do you want to suggest alternatives for Greenline?

Sophia — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to iterate live. If you share the expected ramp schedule, I can populate the 75/150/300 scenarios into the spreadsheet beforehand.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks — a couple of clarifying Qs from procurement/engineering after scanning the proposal:

- Bursts: is the burst cushion applied per month or per rolling-30d window? We have daily flash traffic that could trigger monthly overages if counted per calendar month.
- Rollover: can rollover tokens be used across product lines (we run multiple pipelines under one account)?
- Accounting: if we choose quarterly billing, will we still be able to see line-item usage and credits in the monthly invoice (we need that for internal chargeback)?

If you can confirm those points we can share an internal recommendation to the execs next week.

-Mark

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Annual token commit options for Greenline AI

Hi Mark — quick answers below and proposed next steps.

- Burst window: we design burst cushions to operate on a rolling-30d window by default (reduces calendar-month edge cases). For Greenline’s daily flash patterns that should limit false overages. We can switch to calendar-month if procurement prefers — flag it on the term sheet and we’ll honor that for the contract term.

- Rollover scope: rollover tokens are account-scoped, not product-scoped; Greenline can allocate them across pipelines under the same account ID. We call this out in the MSA and reflect allocation controls in the Console (RBAC) so product teams can claim pools.

- Billing visibility: quarterly billing is fine, and invoices will include line-item usage + credits. Laura — we’ll keep the invoice-level detail identical to monthly reporting so Greenline’s chargeback process is uninterrupted.

Next steps:
1) Rishi and I will update the spreadsheet with stepped Growth tiers (75/150/300) and the proposed two-tier overage schedule.
2) I’ll share a one-page term sheet (non-binding) and a DocuSign link for Greenline’s procurement to review.
3) Schedule 30-min call if you want to walk the numbers live — suggested times attached in the calendar invite (sent separately).

If that aligns, I’ll push the DocuSign and HubSpot term sheet today.

Cheers,
Evelyn
